name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-pulp-timer-zipdma-6w-jumps-f1-fuzz
notes: trigger_writes and status_offsets repeat the values already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-irq-pulp-timer-profile.json; the entry re-checks them against the timer register map and interrupt declarations
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

f1_program_words 6 declares a six-word F1 program in the fixed trampoline slot and f1_allow_jumps admits JAL/JALR with a link destination of x0/x1 and a statically proven target.  A JAL target is kSlot + 4*i + sext(jimm); a JALR target is x[rs1] + sext(imm) and is admitted only when rs1 is x0 or a register the program provably loads one exact constant into (LUI/ADDI/ADD/ANDI).  Every target must be a 4-byte aligned instruction start of the installed image and strictly forward; target == kSlot + 4*words (the appended return jump) is the legal exit.  A backward jump, an indirect base that is not a proven constant, CSR, compressed parcels, loops and out-of-image targets are refused by name.  A jump legally skips words, so the case's evidence is the in-slot RVFI retirement trace: prog_retires and prog_trace_count, the strictly increasing prog_pc_order, prog_pc_repeat 0, and prog_trace_hash (FNV-1a 32 over pc/insn/rd/wdata, including the link-register writeback pc+4) compared with the Python reference trace built from f1_reference_expectation.  Evidence: runs/round1-f1-controlflow/.

fuzz_flows ["F1"] narrows the closed-loop batch to the F1 program flow, so every generated and mutated input is a program of the declared shape whose RVFI retirement trace is compared with the Python reference trace.  The same host/timer/DMA models are built; only the offered flow set changes.
